fatal_errors: The proposed nitrogen-doping treatment is unrelated to the target intervention, which was a closed-loop high-throughput synthesis, post-ageing screening, machine-learning, and Bayesian-optimisation campaign.

The cited evidence concerns electrochemical oxygen reduction on a carbon-supported fuel-cell catalyst, not thermochemical three-way exhaust conversion on La-doped alumina under water-containing 900 °C ageing.
The evidence catalyst required thermal annealing plus acid-etching/dealloying; it does not establish that ammonia annealing alone creates the claimed Pt-rich shell.
Metal–nitrogen stabilization and corrosion resistance under electrochemical conditions are not evidence of stability under highly oxidizing, water-containing automotive exhaust ageing at 900 °C.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses low-PGM activity and durability in broad terms, but it does not reconstruct the intervention, material platform, mechanism, or quantitative outcomes of the target study. It omits the La-doped alumina support, process-variable optimization, Pd and random-search baselines, specified ageing/feed conditions, Cu–Pt reconstruction, hydrocarbon–NO redox coupling, and post-ageing hit-rate results. Its paired treated-versus-untreated experiment is directionally testable and includes useful structural measurements, but the reaction is unspecified, no species-resolved light-off criteria are defined, and it lacks controls separating ammonia exposure, nitrogen incorporation, shell formation, and dealloying. Most importantly, the supporting literature is a substantial domain transfer from fuel-cell ORR and does not validate the proposed exhaust-catalyst mechanism or thermal durability.
